news_analysis.headline_hook: Why LIC's 9.99% ICICI Bank Approval Is NOT an Immediate Buy Signal
news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: The Reserve Bank of India has granted approval to Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to increase its stake in ICICI Bank up to 9.99%.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail traders falsely assume LIC will aggressively buy ICICI Bank shares from the open market starting tomorrow, triggering an immediate runaway rally.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: An RBI approval up to 9.99% is merely a procedural regulatory cap valid for up to one year; institutions buy via off-market block deals or VWAP accumulation over months rather than driving up spot market prices.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Never buy on headline regulatory stake approvals; wait for verified quarterly shareholding pattern updates or off-market block deal prints.

deck.caption:
🚨 STOP chasing the headline. 

When the news hits that LIC got RBI approval to acquire up to 9.99% of ICICI Bank, most retail traders see a 'green candle' rocket ship. 

But here is the institutional truth: An approval is NOT a buy order. It is a regulatory ceiling. 

Institutions don't just 'hit the buy button' on the open market and drive prices up for everyone—they use block deals and VWAP accumulation to keep prices stable while they build their position.

If you buy the headline, you're providing the exit liquidity for the pros. 

Swipe left to see how the 'Institutional Stake-Cap' actually works and why you should wait for the data, not the news. 📉

slides.title: The 'Big Buyer' Illusion
slides.card_a_text: Retail belief: 'LIC got approval for 9.99%, so they will aggressively buy shares tomorrow, triggering a massive rally.'
slides.card_b_text: Institutional reality: RBI approval is a procedural cap, not a purchase order. Buying happens silently via block deals or over months.
slides.takeaway: Headlines create noise. Order flow creates wealth.
slides.body_html:
The Myth: Retail belief: 'LIC got approval for 9.99%, so they will aggressively buy shares tomorrow, triggering a massive rally.'

The Reality: Institutional reality: RBI approval is a procedural cap, not a purchase order. Buying happens silently via block deals or over months.

Core Rule: Headlines create noise. Order flow creates wealth.

slides.title: 3 Reasons Prices Won't Just 'Moon'

points.title: Regulatory Ceiling
points.desc: The 9.99% is a maximum legal limit allowed by the RBI, not a mandatory target LIC must hit immediately.

points.title: Block Deal Preference
points.desc: To avoid 'slippage' (driving the price up against themselves), institutions buy in bulk via off-market transfers.

points.title: VWAP Accumulation
points.desc: Large funds use Volume Weighted Average Price strategies to buy slowly over months, neutralizing spot market spikes.

slides.body_html:
1. Regulatory Ceiling: The 9.99% is a maximum legal limit allowed by the RBI, not a mandatory target LIC must hit immediately.
2. Block Deal Preference: To avoid 'slippage' (driving the price up against themselves), institutions buy in bulk via off-market transfers.
3. VWAP Accumulation: Large funds use Volume Weighted Average Price strategies to buy slowly over months, neutralizing spot market spikes.
